== Biography ==
With so many spelling variations in a variety of sources for Alexander's surname, finding records documenting his life was quite challenging to say the least. What follows was developed from intensive but not exhaustive research. [[Brown-18795|Beth (Brown) Golden]] 1:30 EST, 23 April 2024

=== Birth ===
Most accounts of Reverend Alexander Hutcheson agree that he was born about 1630 - 1640 in Scotland. Alexander was <b>not</b> born in Monkwood, Ayrshire. The Hutcheson family did not own that land until 1703.<ref>Paterson, James. “Parish of Maybole” History of the Counties of Ayr and Wigton, Volume 2  pp. 442-443 https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=o10LAAAAYAAJ&pg=GBS.PA72&hl=en</ref> An alternate, but similar location is Monkton, found in his profile in the <u>Fasti of the Irish Presbyterian Church, 1613-1840</u><ref> FamilySearch https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/records/item/833408-fasti-of-the-irish-presbyterian-church-1613-1840?offset=17 pp. 40-41 BEWARE of this source, as it has citations that are incorrect and misinformation.</ref> Many manuscripts state that his father was George. Unless Alexander had a son prior to John, Alexander's father was likely named John, following Scottish naming patterns.

The approximate birth year of 1640 seems to be correct based on allowing him enough time to attend university prior to serving the first Presbyterian Church in Saintfield, Down, Northern Ireland. However, no Ayrshire birth/baptismal record was found for Alexander Hutcheson (with spelling variations) in the Old Parish Registers held by Scotland's People. However, 2 were found occurring in Edinburgh<ref> Scotland's People, Old Parish Registers, Births/Baptisms https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/advanced-search/church_registers/opr_births#form</ref>:
*HUTCHESONE, ALEXANDER son of WILLIAME HUTCHESONE/AGNES NOBLE on 06/10/1639<br>
*HUTCHESONE, ALEXANDER son of ISAAC HUTCHESONE/MAUSE BOOK on 22/01/1643<br>

Several other births are listed throughout Scotland between 1632 and 1648.

In the 1640s, Rev. George Hutcheson of Calmonell, Dumfries-Galloway (an early association with Glencairn), was a compatriot of Rev. John Livingstone.<ref>Tweedie, Rev. W. K. Select Biographies, Volume 1 The Life of Mr. John Livingstone; Wodrow Society, Edinburgh, 1845. https://archive.org/details/selectbiographies01twee/page/150/mode/2up? pp. 168, 169 and 260.</ref> In 1695, Janet Hutcheson was listed in the Hearth Tax Roll for Cabreth and James Hutchison in Stranraer, both in Wigtownshire, Galloway, Scotland.<ref>Kerr, Andrew Thomas (2009) The significance of the Wigtownshire Hearth Tax lists. MPhil(R) thesis. http://theses.gla.ac.uk/2786/ </ref>

Note that Patrik Dicksone married Bessie Hutchesone in Edinburgh Parish on 17/08/1603.<ref>Old Parish Records, Scotland's People, Marriages</ref> Their children: Catharine baptized 23/07/1612 and Thomas baptized 01/08/1613, both in Edinburgh Parish. No later children were  listed.<ref>Old Parish Records, Scotland's People, Births and Baptisms</ref> The Testament of Patrick, an indweller of Edinburgh, was filed 21/011/16433 Patrick may be related to the William and Isaac and Bessie to Alexander of this biography.<ref>Scotland's People Legal Testament https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/advanced-search/legal-records#record-type </ref>

It is more likely that Mr. Hutcheson was born in County Down.  Hutcheson men were also mustered throughout County Down in the 1600s. In 1633, Robert and Patrick Hutcheson were listed on the Muster Roll for Lord Clandeboy (Sir James Hamilton), both owning a sword, musket and bandolier.<ref>Hunter, R. J.; <u>Men and Arms: The Ulster Settlers, c. 1630</u>; Ulster Historical Foundation, 27 Jan 2015. http://www.therjhuntercollection.com/resources/muster-rolls-c-1630/  accessed 22 April 2024 via Hoopla through Dekalb County Library</ref>Patrick and Robert are the most likely relatives of Rev. Hutcheson since while living in the townland of Lisdalgan, he purchased the nearby townland of Drumalig (located approximately 16 miles south-west of Bangor) from James Hamilton about 20 years later.

No birth or baptismal records have been found to date to fully document Rev. Hutcheson's birth.

=== Education ===
For a few years, Rev. Hutcheson attended the University of Glasgow beginning in 1650 and then attended St. Andrews University. He was taught by Prof. Samuel Rutherford, a Covenanting hero. He matriculated on 4 February 1653 and graduated with an M.A. on 13 May 1653 from the College of St. Leonard's (Divinity).<ref>Pearson, A. F. Scott. “Alumni of St. Andrews and the Settlement of Ulster.” Ulster Journal of Archaeology, vol. 14, 1951, pp. 7–14. JSTOR, http://www.jstor.org/stable/20566629 p. 5 Accessed 29 Mar. 2024. This article also has information on the Reverends Blair of Bangor, several Hamiltons including James of Ballywalter, John Livingstone of Killinchy in 1630, all graduates of St. Andrews. </ref>

=== Residence in Down ===
He acquired Drumalig in 1671 from Viscount Clandeboy, AKA Lord Clanbrassil (Sir James Hamilton, grandson of Sir James who established the Scots settlement in Ulster along with Sir Hugh Montgomery). Mr. Wauchop was the other party of this tripartite land indenture. Another source incorrectly stated that it was a marriage gift. The actual deed does not mention Mr. Hutcheson's wife, nor is it a marriage settlement. Rather, Rev. Hutchinson [sic] of Lisdalgan, Tonaghneve paid ₤300 for Drumalig. This land deed was entered into the official register on 30 May 1671.<ref>NAI Lodge/7/643, 'Deed between Lord Clanbrassil and ALEXANDER HUTCHINSON of lands in Down'. Accessed on Virtual Record Treasury of Ireland https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-Lodge-7-643 (accessed 3 April 2024). Repository: National Archives, Ireland.</ref>

=== Wife and Children ===
The wife of Mr. Hutcheson has not been identified as of this writing. She was not mentioned in his Will/Testament, so presumably she died prior to 20 January 1711. One Alexander Hutcheson married Alison Borthwike on 2 July 1675 in Edinburgh.<ref>Carson, Ann. “Borthwick Marriages in Scotland, pre-1857 “ https://freepages.rootsweb.com/~anncarson/genealogy/Borthwick/borthwickmarriagesoprsct.htm </ref> He may be the same man as this profile. DNA analysis of Mr. Hutcheson's descendants may reveal the identity of his wife.

They had at least two daughters and one son:<ref>Betham, William. FamilySearch catalogue listing https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog/224404?availability=Family%20History%20Library</ref> <ref>http://freepages.rootsweb.com/~alanmilliken/genealogy/Research/IrishRecords/CountiesIreland/Ballyholme1.html</ref>
*Alexander's elder daughter, Beatrix, married Hugh Wallace of Ballyobikin and Ravara, Down. Beatrix was likely born in Drumalig, Saintfield, County Down. She married Hugh Wallace about 1684. He was likely of the same family of Hugh Wallace, Esquire who owned the townland of Roddans, Ballyhalbert in 1659. A later family member was Hester Wallace, a spinster, who lived in Saintfield in 1798. She petitioned and received  claimed £49 8p 10s compensation from the government for the loss of clothes, furniture, plate & web from her residence during the 1798 Rebellion. In the mid 1700s, several men named Hugh Wallace were living in Killinchy and Ravara. They were sons of James Wallace and mentioned in land deeds between 1733 and 1750. In 1780, one Hugh Wallace of Saintfield, had his Will probated<ref>Ros Davies Surnames Wallace https://www.rosdavies.com/SURNAMES/W/WallaceAJ.htm</ref> <br>
*Alexander's youngest daughter, Mary, born in Drumalig, married John Young of Listooder and Ballydian in the parish of Kilmore, County Down. By a deed dated 16th October, 1728, James Young of Belfast merchant and Jane Young alias Milliken his wife, sold to the Rev. Samuel Hutchinson of Ballygraffan in the parish of Ballyhalbert, county of Down, the lands of Fishers Quarter lying in the barony of Ards, together with the parsonage and rectoral of the said lands of Fisher Quarter.<ref>McCosh, James. The Scottish Philosophy Biographical, Expository, Critical From Hutcheson to Hamilton James McCosh, LL.D., D.D., President of The College of New Jersey, Princeton; London: Macmillan And Co. 1875 https://historyofeconomicthought.mcmaster.ca/mccosh/scottishphilosophy.pdf Citing in Notes Section: 10. “Account of the Life, Writings, and Character of Francis Hutcheson,” by William Leechman, D.D., prefixed to Hutcheson’s “Moral Philosophy;” Carlyle’s “Autobiography;” MSS. Letters from Hutcheson to Dr Drennan, etc.</ref><br>
*His son, John, born in Drumalig, Saintfield (noted in Fasti as “only” but other source states “surviving”) was minister in Downpatrick (1690 – 1697) and Armagh (1697-10 February 1729).<ref>Wikitree https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hutcheson-360 Death date from <u>History Congregations of the Presbyterian Church in Ireland and Biographical Notices of Eminent Presbyterian Ministers and Laymen</u></ref> Interestingly, Mr. Archibald Hamilton, <i>son of James Hamilton, of Ballywalter, loosed from his charge in Benburb, in May, 1673, and thereafter settled in Armagh. At the time of the troubles in 1688, he retired to Scotland, and afterwards in 1692, at his own request, the Synod dissolved his connection with this [Armagh] congregation. He was then settled as minister at Killinchy in 1693.</i><ref>Killen, W. D., comp. <u>History of congregations of the Presbyterian Church in Ireland and biographical notices of eminent Presbyterian ministers and laymen, with the signification of names of places</u>; Belfast, 1886. https://archive.org/details/historyofcongreg00kill/</ref> He was the father of eminent Rev. Francis Hutcheson.<ref>Rev. Francis Hutchinson/Hutcheson, Alexander's grandson was quite influential. http://discoversaintfield.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/04/2000_Orr_Mr_Hutcheson.pdf,  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Hutcheson_(philosopher)  and https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hutcheson-359 </ref> Mr. John Hutcheson is mentioned numerous times in the Synod of Ulster records.<ref>Records of the General Synod of Ulster, from 1691 to 1820, Volume 1 Google Books https://g.co/kgs/abAZAS3</ref> <i>John, was settled at Ballyrea, within two miles of Artnagh, and ministered to a Presbyterian congregation in the archiepis opal city, where he was known by his church as a man of retiring habits and of superior abilities, and a firm supporter of Calvinistic doctrine. His second son, Francis, was born Aug. 8, 1694, it is said in his grandfather’s house in Drumalig. When about eight years of age, he (with his elder brother, Hans) was put under the care of the same grandfather, and attended a classical school kept by Mr Hamilton in the “meeting house” at Saintfield. He was afterwards sent to Killyleagh, in the same county, to an academy kept by the Rev. James Macalpin, said to be a man of virtue and ability, and who taught the future metaphysician the scholastic philosophy.</i><ref>McCosh, James. The Scottish Philosophy Biographical, Expository, Critical From Hutcheson to Hamilton James McCosh, LL.D., D.D., President of The College of New Jersey, Princeton; London: Macmillan And Co. 1875 https://historyofeconomicthought.mcmaster.ca/mccosh/scottishphilosophy.pdf</ref> The family of John Hutcheson (2)<ref>“Armachiana Volume 10; Jun 3, 2020  https://issuu.com/acdcdesign/docs/_armachianavol10 </ref> His first wife, whose name is not known at this time, likely died in Armagh. His known children:
*Hans born about 1692 who had no children and Francis born 8 August 1694 possibly in Drumalig. <br>
*John, after the death of his first wife, married Miss Wilson, daughter of Francis of Tully, County Longford, possibly his cousin. She likely died in Armagh or Dublin. His son, Francis, was the only survivor of 7 children. He became the esteemed and eminent minister and philosopher.<br>

=== Employment ===
Alexander Hutcheson, the first minister of Tonaghneave Presbyterian Church, County Down (now Saintfield) appears not be listed in the Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae,<ref>Ecclegen, General Index  https://www.ecclegen.com/general-index-h/#Huston,%20Samuel%3C </ref> implying that he did not hold a ministerial position in Scotland. After graduating from St. Andrews, he returned to County Down as a probationer and joined the Presbytery of Down. He was ordained in Tonaghneeve in 1657. Initially he was not paid but on 29 Sept 1659 the Presbytery ordered that he receive £25. Later on he received £100 a year from the Protectorate. In 1661 he was deposed for non-conformity by Bishop Jeremy Taylor but continued to minister. About this time we was accused of being involved with Blood's Plot of 1663 and imprisoned. By 1690, Mr. Hutcheson supplied Capel Street (on Rutland Square, Dublin) and elected as Moderator of the General Synod.<ref>Moderators of the General Synod https://presbyterianhistoryireland.com/web-resources/lists/moderators-of-the-synod-of-ulster-1690-1840/ </ref> He remained there until April 1692.  At the Synod of 1691 there were commissioners from Saintfield — viz.. Captain Gawin Hamilton, Messrs. Robert Ross, Robert Kyle, John Hamilton, and others, supplicating the return of Mr. Hutchinson, and the Synod of 1692 granted the application. He now continued here till his death in 1711. He served as Moderator of the General Synod between 1692-93. In June 1708, being elderly and ill, he demitted his charge at Tonaghneeve.<ref>https://pure.ulster.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/104388246/2022BellLPhD.pdf Citing Records of the General Synod of Ulster, p. 97.</ref> <ref>Killen, W. D., comp. History of congregations of the Presbyterian Church in Ireland and biographical notices of eminent Presbyterian ministers and laymen, with the signification of names of places; Belfast, 1886. Compiled by W. D. Killen, from original work done by Rev. J. S. Reid, D.D., before his appointment as Professor of Ecclesiastical and Civil History in the University of Glasgow, at the request of Rev. Reid's executors. Rev. James Seaton Reid was born in Lurgan, Down on 19 December 1798 to Forrest and Mary Reid. He died 26 March 1851. His connection to Rev. James Reid of Killinchy is not known at this time. https://archive.org/details/historyofcongreg00kill/page/226/mode/2up?view=theater</ref>

It appears that he spent some time in Edinburgh, for between 1658 and 1662 numerous marriages were officiated by Rev. Alexander Hutcheson(e) in the Holyrood Kirk portion of Canongate Church.<ref>Canongate Marriages http://www.archive.org/details/scottishrecordso34scotuoft </ref> The marriages performed by Hutcheson are distinguished from most entries because they list him specifically, where many other entries do not list a minister. Hutcheson was a guest and not the official minister of Canongate during this time, so it is likely that he was invited by either the bride or groom.<ref>Wikipedia Canongate Kirk https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canongate_Kirk </ref> Of particular note because of the surname associations with others in County Down, especially in Ballynahinch prior to 18003 were:
*1658 Christina Manson to John DICKSON, a cook<br>
*1659 Alan Mannering [Manning?], Englishman to Margaret AITKEN [Aiken, spelling variations]<br>
*1661 with George REID to Margaret Brown<br>
*1662 with Elspeth REID to Andro Sym(m)er [Sime?]<br>

Rev. Hutcheson is mentioned numerous times in the Synod of Ulster records<ref>Records of the General Synod of Ulster, from 1691 to 1820, Volume 1 Google Books https://g.co/kgs/abAZAS3 </ref>

=== Will and Probate ===
Rev. Hutcheson wrote his Will on 7 January 1711 while living in Tonaghneave.<ref>PRONI Ref# T/403 p.43 https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ </ref> It appears that the actual testament is not available online. He left his home and estate in Drumalig to his grandson, Francis, bypassing his eldest grandson, Hans, and his own children's families. Francis declined the gift in favor of his brother Hans, but Hans also declined. In the end, they agreed to share the inheritance between them.<ref>Herman, Arthur. How the Scots Invented the Modern World; Three Rivers Press, NY; 2002. p. 71 Extensive discussion of Francis Hutcheson contained in this book beginning on page 65.</ref> According to Betham, the Will was filed on 5 September 1711.<ref>Betham, William. "Ireland, Betham Genealogical Abstracts, 1179-1830", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L9LW-6Z5B?cc=4496119  : 26 December 2023), > image 1 of 1. Betham's abstract from Series 1 Wills Volume 17 “D” Image 180 (p. 121-122 in document). FamilySearch catalogue listing https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog/224404?availability=Family%20History%20Library</ref>

=== Death and Burial ===
Mr. Hutcheson died before 5 September 1711<ref>Synod of Ulster records</ref>while staying with his son, John, who was minister of the 1st Presbyterian Church in Armagh. It is unknown whether Rev. Alexander was buried there or brought to his home in Tonaghneave/Saintfield. His burial is not listed in Clarke's Gravestones of County Down, Volumes 1-5<ref>Clarke R. S. J and Ulster Historical Foundation. Gravestone Inscriptions; Belfast, Ulster Historical Foundation; 1982. </ref>, FindAGrave<ref>https://www.findagrave.com/ </ref>, or BillionGraves.<ref>https://billiongraves.com/ </ref>

== Research Notes ==
A possible identification concerns Eupham Glasgow and Alexander Hutcheson. The parish index records Eupham Glasgow with Alexander Hutcheson at Edinburgh on 8 December 1671.<ref>Scotland’s People, Old Parish Registers, banns and marriages, OPR 685 / 1/440 / 129, 1671-12-08, Edinburgh; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The index combines banns and marriage entries; the original register is required to establish the event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Effie Glasgow and Alexander Hutcshesone. The parish index records Effie Glasgow with Alexander Hutcshesone at Channelkirk on 17 September 1671.<ref>Scotland’s People, Old Parish Registers, banns and marriages, OPR 729/10 / 230, 1671-09-17, Channelkirk; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The index combines banns and marriage entries; the original register is required to establish the event type. The identification remains uncertain.
